method: The input is 48 kHz, stereo PCM16. I kept samples in 0-2 s and 24-26 s bit-identical. Across 2-24 s I formed mid/side signals, estimated the clean protected-window side-to-mid spectral ratio from 0.08-1.92 s, smoothed the estimate across frequency, and used a conservative time-frequency Wiener attenuation with 4096-sample Hann windows, 512-sample hop, and smoothed gains. The stereo side estimate is anchored to the protected-window ratio; gains were bounded to avoid spectral nulls. The restored WAV was written as 48 kHz stereo PCM16. The AV preview uses that WAV with AAC at 512 kbit/s.
limitations: No audio-perception tool is available in this session, so I did not listen to the result and make no subjective sound-quality claim. No clean reference waveform or fixed onset/damage-event locations were available. Observations below are signal measurements; they do not establish reference-relative SNR, onset fidelity, or perceptual artifact removal. The mid/side prior can attenuate genuine stereo width when the music's spatial content differs from the protected windows.
